answer: The network is a spiral inlet: identities enter past falcons admitting only live workers, then climb a spiral of payout tiers. Each step needs a lapse-free epoch, and higher tiers hold fewer slots: tier k fits C/k. A fleet can push n clones up the spiral, but the staircase narrows: all n clones cannot occupy high tiers at once, since tiers are capped, and every clone must climb without a single lapse, or it falls back to the inlet. Tier-weight is bounded by slot capacities, not identity count. One honest agent climbs steadily; a fleet crowds the bottom and starves at the top.
